metadata.summary: Britain's Jodie Burrage has received death threats and abuse on social media after she was beaten in the first round of the Chennai Open on Tuesday.
metadata.content: Jodie Burrage: British player receives death threats and abuse on social media after Chennai Open first-round defeat | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Jodie Burrage: British player receives death threats and abuse on social media after Chennai Open first-round defeat Jodie Burrage has revealed online abuse and death threats; both Burrage and fellow British player Katie Boulter believe most abuse comes from tennis gamblers who have lost money; Warning: This article contains details some readers may find distressing Tuesday 3 November 2026 22:34, UK Image: Jodie Burrage has received death threats and abuse on social media following her defeat at the Chennai Open Britain's Jodie Burrage has received death threats and abuse on social media after she was beaten in the first round of the Chennai Open on Tuesday. Burrage, who was playing her first WTA Tour singles match in 16 months, went down against India's Vaishnavi Adkar. She looked poised for victory when she led 5-3 in the deciding set but lost four games in a row to fall to a 3-6 6-3 7-5 defeat after two hours and 47 minutes. The 27-year-old, who reached a career-high ranking 85 in September 2023, published an Instagram story with some of the abuse received due to the defeat. messages.text: Esteve hoping for Champions League debut – and Haaland reunion

metadata.summary: A reunion with Manchester City brings bad memories for the RB Leipzig defender Maxime Esteve. He scored two own goals at the Etihad Stadium last year. Not that he has advertised this to his new teammates. "Maybe they don't even know," he jokes.
metadata.content: Maxime Esteve interview: RB Leipzig defender on his Erling Haaland reunion after two own goals against Man City | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Maxime Esteve interview: RB Leipzig defender on his Erling Haaland reunion after two own goals against Man City Maxime Esteve is hoping to make his Champions League debut against Manchester City and Erling Haaland, the man he rates as the best striker in the world. In this interview, he discusses working with Vincent Kompany at Burnley and his new life at RB Leipzig… Adam Bate Football Features Writer @ghostgoal Tuesday 3 November 2026 19:05, UK Image: RB Leipzig defender Maxime Esteve faces Manchester City in the Champions League A reunion with Manchester City brings bad memories for the RB Leipzig defender Maxime Esteve. He scored two own goals at the Etihad Stadium last year. Not that he has advertised this to his new teammates. "Maybe they don't even know," he jokes. It is an amusing statistic that this time last year, indeed until the final days of November, a dozen games into the Premier League season, Esteve had found the net for City more times than everyone bar Erling Haaland. "This is a secret. You don't have to say!" The 24-year-old French centre-back left Burnley for Leipzig in the summer and the truth is that he is aching to face City again.
